title: Choose the visual world for M J Cargo Movers
question: The roll assigned The Expressway Out of Panvel. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Expressway Out of Panvel
options.lineage: Mumbai–Pune Expressway road surface: night asphalt, thermoplastic lane paint, overhead gantry signs
options.thesis: The site is the road your goods take: night-navy asphalt, painted lane lines, and gantry signs that ask where your cargo is going.
options.viewport: Full-bleed night-navy field; a wide gantry-style headline 'Moving your cargo forward, with confidence'; the real Mumbai goods-carrier photograph large on the right; a thick dashed amber lane line runs from 'New Panvel' toward a working 'Where is it going?' pickup → delivery quote starter.
options.risk: Road paint can tip into costume if the lane motif appears in every section instead of carrying the route once.

raised.raise: The ground steps from night navy (booking) to daylight white (delivery) as the visitor moves down the process, so colour carries state.
Amber is reserved for the active leg only: the primary action and the visitor's own consignment line, nowhere decorative.
One unambiguous state vocabulary: controls invert navy↔white when pressed or selected.
One consignment held at a time: the quote form keeps a live summary of the single load being described.
Every visible fact traces to a source; unverified details stay out instead of being decorated in.

options.label: The Lorry Receipt
options.lineage: the bilty / LR consignment note every trader has filled in
options.thesis: The website is the consignment note: boxed fields for consignor, consignee, from, to, packages and weight, stamped by the agent.
options.viewport: A large LR form sheet as the hero, its From/To boxes live inputs, the company stamp in amber beside the headline.
options.risk: The most familiar reading of a cargo agent; boxed form grids fight the house rule against thin rules.

options.label: Claim and Proof
options.thesis: Each claim about the service is followed by the concrete proof: address, process, the form itself.
options.viewport: Near-white page, tight sans headline, one amber action, photograph framed beside it.
options.case: Holds product clarity; loses audience identification, since Panvel traders don't read software pages, and there is little proof to pair yet.
options.risk: Reads like a SaaS template; thin on proof for a business with no published statistics.

options.label: Cyclorama Dawn
options.thesis: Night to day as a lit horizon.
options.viewport: Dark stage with a cobalt horizon band.
options.case: Fuses poorly: traders don't identify with stagecraft; rose fights the pinned palette.
options.kept: State carried by ground colour, night to day.

options.label: Orienteering Map
options.thesis: Routes as a course over terrain.
options.viewport: Terrain map with a purple course.
options.case: Would need route data the company hasn't confirmed; purple fights the brief.
options.kept: One colour reserved for the active leg.

options.label: One-bit Desktop
options.case: No connection to road freight buyers.
options.kept: Pressing inverts: one clear state language.

options.label: Event Display
options.thesis: One event held at a time.
options.case: Alien to the audience; heavy WebGL hurts phones on mobile data.
options.kept: One consignment held at a time.

options.label: Jacquard Brocade
options.viewport: Midnight silk with a gold motif.
options.case: Luxury textile register misreads a cargo agent.
options.kept: Every visible element traceable to its source.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A logistics company site: truck photo hero, three service cards, process steps, contact form, executed at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Headline left, truck photo right, quote button, service cards below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other transporter's site by design.
